stem: In physical architecture, how do statutory minimum building standards differ from universal design best practices?

options.text: Statutory minimum standards pursue full inclusion, while universal design practices focus on basic legal compliance.
options.shortLabel: Minimums pursue inclusion; UD is basic
options.rationale: The relationship is the opposite: minimum standards define baseline legal compliance, while universal design pursues fuller inclusion.

options.text: Statutory minimum standards apply mainly to housing, whereas universal design applies mainly to transport hubs.
options.rationale: Building standards apply across public and commercial structures, and universal design applies to all building types.

options.text: Minimum standards treat ramps as optional, whereas universal design requires dedicated elevators.
options.rationale: Minimum building codes require an accessible route, so ramps are not optional extras; universal design does not single out elevators.

options.text: Minimum codes set a legal baseline, while universal design aims for optimal usability for everyone.
options.rationale: Minimum codes establish mandatory baselines often framed as individual accommodation, while universal design strives for seamless, barrier-free access.

explanation: Minimum building codes set the enforceable baseline necessary to satisfy legal compliance, which often results in isolated accommodations (like a separate side entrance ramp). Universal design best practice guidelines encourage design that exceeds minimum thresholds to create intuitive, dignified, and integrated spaces for all users.

references.title: Centre for Universal Design Australia: Minimum access standards and myths
